Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which factor increases as stream velocity decreases. The options are erosion of the stream bank, deposition of material, amount of material carried downstream, and size of the particles carried downstream. 

First, I remember that stream velocity affects how much sediment is transported. When the velocity is high, the stream can carry more sediment because the water has more energy to pick up and move particles. But when velocity decreases, the stream's ability to transport sediment also decreases. This makes me think that the amount of material carried downstream would go down, so maybe option C is not the answer.

Next, I think about what happens to the stream bank when velocity drops. I recall that during times of lower flow, the stream bank can become more prone to erosion. This is because the water has less force, so it can't hold the bank as well. The bank might become saturated, and without the same pressure from the flowing water, the soil and particles can erode more easily. So, this makes me consider that option A, erosion of the stream bank, might be the correct answer.

I also consider deposition. When velocity is high, the water is more turbulent, which can cause more sediment to be deposited because the water slows down and drops. But when velocity decreases, the water is calmer, so maybe less sediment is deposited in the stream. That would mean option B, deposition of material, might decrease, so it's not the answer.

Regarding the size of the particles carried downstream, I think that when velocity is lower, the water can't carry as much sediment, and the particles might be smaller because the flow isn't as strong. But I'm not entirely sure if this is a direct effect or if it's more about the total amount carried. I need to think more about this.

Putting it all together, the main factor that increases when velocity decreases is likely the erosion of the stream bank because the lower flow can't hold the bank as well, leading to more erosion. The amount carried downstream and the size of particles might also be affected, but the most significant increase is in bank erosion.
</think>
